title: Terms of Spending an Upgrade Credit under the Belrose Trade-In and Upgrade Programmes
content:
## Conditions in force

(a) Credit is spent only against the sale it is presented for, identified by the till transaction number and the merchandise line the credit was applied to. Both identifiers are those recorded for the spend, and a credit is never applied to a sale other than the one those identifiers name.

(b) Credit is spent only while the registration stands at credit issued or partially redeemed, and never against a registration that has closed. The standing is read from the registration before the spend.

(c) On the programmes that allow it the credit may be spent in parts across several sales; on the programmes that do not, it is spent once and anything left over is lost.

(d) Credit is spent on merchandise and, where the programme admits it, on a protection plan, on workshop work or on a custom commission; the programmes that do not admit those do not spend credit on them.

(e) Credit is never taken as money except under the programme that offers an outright purchase, and a customer asking for cash against an upgrade credit is told so plainly.

(f) Where the programme admits it, the credit may be applied against a financed balance instead of at the till, and the financing desk posts it as a credit to that plan.

The multiple, the uplift, whether the credit may be spent in parts, what it may be spent on, whether it may offset a financed balance, whether it may be taken as money, whether it may be transferred and whether the new piece must be of the same or a higher grade are the programme's published figures under the Belrose Trade-In and Upgrade Programmes.

## Condition no longer in force

The following condition is **no longer in force** and has been superseded by the current basis for the least the customer must spend: "Credit is spent only against a new piece costing at least the programme's multiple of the credit, and on the programmes that also require an uplift, at least that much more than the piece traded originally sold for." Under that withdrawn condition the smallest price for the new piece was the higher of the credit issued taken at the programme's multiple, rounded to two decimal places, and the original selling price raised by the programme's uplift, rounded to two decimal places. The programme's published multiple and uplift remain the programme's figures.

## Questions on the conditions

**May a credit be spent on a repair?** Only where the programme admits workshop work; where it does not, no credit goes to the workshop.

**May a customer take the credit in cash?** No, except under the programme that offers an outright purchase; under every other programme the customer is told so plainly.

**What happens to what is left of a once-only credit?** It is lost. Under a programme that allows part-spending, what is left stays on the registration.

superseded_clauses: Credit is spent only against a new piece costing at least the programme's multiple of the credit, and on the programmes that also require an uplift, at least that much more than the piece traded originally sold for.
